what_happened: The person running Athena deleted by hand the 9.7 GB writer build folder of job 20261102-154551-5qcd, the core-test-split job. The job was held on low disk, not failed. No acceptance criterion, check or finding failed. The free-space check runs before the job's own regenerable build is removed, so the job was held because of its own build. This is the fourth hold from this ordering. The fix for the ordering is mid-retry and has not landed.
cause: Athena has no disk lifecycle tied to a build's own state. The free-space guard counts a regenerable build as space the job still needs, and the step that removes that build runs later. The hold only waits and reclaims nothing, so a held job's own build blocks its resume. The fix is an ordinary queued job that needs the same disk, so the fault delays its own repair. The fix has no priority and no exemption from the guard, and held jobs are not resumed automatically. Each repeat therefore needs a hand cleanup.
prevention: Make the disk guard and build cleanup one ordered step. Before the free-space check, and again on any low-disk hold, Athena removes the regenerable builds of held, interrupted and finished jobs, then measures free space. Only the unfreeable shortfall holds a job. Held jobs resume automatically once space is available. The repair job for this fault runs first and is exempt from the guard until it lands. Test it with a job whose own 10 GB build would otherwise cause the hold.
proposed_request: Fix the disk guard so a job is never held on low disk because of its own regenerable build. Outcome: when free space is below the limit, Athena first removes regenerable builds that no running job needs (held, interrupted and finished jobs, including the job's own writer build) and re-measures. It holds a job only if space is still short afterward, and says how much is short. Held jobs resume automatically when free space recovers. The hold records of earlier batches are not skipped. Run this fix ahead of the other queued jobs, and do not apply the disk guard to it while its own build is the cause. Acceptance: a test where a job's own 10 GB regenerable build would fall below the limit passes the guard after cleanup. A test where space stays short after cleanup holds the job with a message that gives the shortfall. A held job resumes in a later drain without a hand command. The jobs 20261102-154551-5qcd and its dependents continue from their kept work.
